successors.note: Antes page: 'In 602 ... the Avars sent their general Apsich' to 'destroy the nation of the Antes'; they 'never again appear in sources, apart from the epithet Anticus in the imperial titulature in 612'. Kazanski dates the downfall to the first half of the 7th century, with Bulgar and then Khazar arrivals; possible heirs 'Croats, Drevlians, Dulebes, Polans, Severians, Tiverians and Ulichians' (uncertain). The avar-khaganate dossier gives the Avars the Dniester-Dnieper steppe until 656 (event 14), which supports the successor.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 518-602: the Antes between the Dniester and the Dnieper. 'They lived on the lower Danube River, in the northwestern Black Sea region (present-day Moldova and central Ukraine), and in the regions around the Don River'; 'The Antes were based between the Bug and lower Dnieper in the 1st-2nd centuries CE'; Jordanes has them 'along the curve of the Black Sea' from the Dniester to the Dnieper; 'the Antes stretched well across Sarmatian Scythia, rather than being a small and distant polity'. The page gives no area or boundary; Odessa and Mykolayiv oblasts plus Moldova (about 91,000 km2) are a reading of the Dniester-Dnieper phrase, leaving out the Don and the interior ('central Ukraine'), where the page's ranges are vaguer. The avar-khaganate shape of 561 (655,633 km2, the lower Danube basin and the Pontic steppe) covers this land from 561; the ledger marks 562-602 as contested. Infobox area: none on the page.

ledger.note: 518: the Antes first appear in the Roman record. 'The first contact between the Eastern Romans and the Antes was in 518 CE.' The page has no founding of a state: 'Although the Antes are regarded as a predominantly Slavic tribal union', it lists an earlier king Boz (fl. 376-80), crucified with seventy nobles after a battle with Vinitharius (undated), and nothing between 380 and 518. The year is the first attestation, a bridge.

ledger.note: About 562: the Avars and the Antes fight. 'They were often involved in conflicts with the Avars' (560s, recorded by Menander); 'Mezamir (fl. 562), powerful Antae archon'. The Pannonian Avars page (Pohl): 'for 20 years to come the Avars, under their Khagan Baian, fought Utigurs and Antes, Gepids and Slavs', and that they 'defeated the Antes'. The page dates no battle; 562 is the year the page gives for Mezamir.

wars.name: Antes invasion of the Diocese of Thrace
wars.outcome: 'Sometime between 533 and 545, the Antes invaded the Diocese of Thrace, enslaving many Romans'; in 545 they 'became Roman allies (after approaching the Romans) and were given gold payments' and a fort named Turris, location uncertain.
wars.note: A raid, no land changed hands; the page does not date it closer than 533-545. Chilbudius, a Roman commander, 'was killed three years later during an expedition against the various Sklavenoi'.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks, requested by eu-06-f (counterparts_needing_dossiers 'Antes', 'eu-06-x or eu-18'). Four pages opened (the Antes page twice). A Slavic tribal union, not a state with a documented territory: its start (518, the first Roman contact) and end (602) are the dates at which the sources name it, and the region is a reading of the Dniester-Dnieper phrase; events 518, 562 and 602 are confidence 1-2. Boz (fl. 376-80) and the Antes of the 1st-2nd centuries between the Bug and the lower Dnieper are on the page but not drawn: nothing dates a polity between 380 and 518, and the gothia dossier (207-382) covers the Cherniakhov land. The page notes the Antes 'in the regions around the Don River' (not drawn). The sclaviniae-of-greece dossier (eu-05-x) is the Slavic settlement of Greece, a different thing. The avar-khaganate shape of 561 (655,633 km2) overlaps this land; the contest 562-602 is the reading that avoids drawing the Avars as sole holders. Rulers named: Boz, Dabragezas, Idariz, Mezamir, Kelagast, none with reign years. Wikidata id unknown.
